quote: Although human evaluation remains the gold standard for assessing summary quality and readability, the high cost and slow turnaround have led many researchers to rely on automatic evaluation metrics for evaluating PLS summaries.

We consider 8 readability metrics: Flesh-Kincaid Grade Level (FKGL), Flesch Reading Ease (FRE), Dale Chall Readability Score (DCRS), Automated Readability Index (ARI), Coleman Liau Index (CLI), Gunning Fog Index (GFI), Spache and Linsear Write (LW).
The majority of prior work use a combination of readability metrics, such as Flesch Reading Ease or the Gunning-Fog Index to validate the readability of their dataset or generations.
we explore whether LMs can judge the readability of a summary.
We experiment with 5 LMs as evaluators of readability... All of the LMs outperform the traditional metrics.
We experiment with 5 LMs as evaluators of readability: Mistral 7B, Mixtral 7B, Gemma 7B, Llama 3.1 8B, and Llama 3.3 70B.
methods: scoring readability on a 1 to 5 scale

quote: This dataset contains 60 summaries of 10 scientific papers... annotated on a scale of 1 to 5 for the annotator's reading ease.
Each summary is annotated on a scale of 1 to 5 for the annotator's reading ease of the article. 1 indicates a very poor reading ease, while 5 indicates a very high reading ease.
Each paper has both expert written and machine written summaries (generated using GPT-3.) The summaries are annotated on a scale of 1 to 5 for the annotator's reading ease of the article.
